catalog: its visits take 2 call shapes, modelled as a mixture (it calls each shape with the share of visits that took it): index-a + index-b + index-c + index-d (23.1% of visits); inventory (23.1% of visits)

features: its visits take 4 call shapes, modelled as a mixture (it calls each shape with the share of visits that took it): feature-store x5 (26.0% of visits); feature-store x6 (25.1% of visits); feature-store x4 (24.9% of visits); feature-store x3 (23.9% of visits)
features -> feature-store: calls per visit vary as {3: 1791, 4: 1871, 5: 1953, 6: 1885}; the call shapes carry them (4.52 per visit on average)

feed: its visits take 9 call shapes, modelled as a mixture (it calls each shape with the share of visits that took it): profile then graph then media x4 then rank (11.5% of visits); profile then graph then media x12 then rank (11.5% of visits); profile then graph then media x6 then rank (11.4% of visits); profile then graph then media x10 then rank (11.4% of visits); profile then graph then media x11 then rank (11.2% of visits); profile then graph then media x7 then rank (11.0% of visits); profile then graph then media x8 then rank (10.7% of visits); profile then graph then media x9 then rank (10.7% of visits); profile then graph then media x5 then rank (10.6% of visits)
feed -> media: calls per visit vary as {4: 1043, 5: 957, 6: 1034, 7: 997, 8: 973, 9: 968, 10: 1033, 11: 1012, 12: 1040}; the call shapes carry them (8.01 per visit on average)

graph -> graph-store: calls per visit vary as {1: 2992, 2: 3087, 3: 2978}; only their mean (2 per visit) enters the model, as 1 call(s) made on every visit and one more with probability 1.00. That is exact for the load on graph-store and for the mean time of a caller that makes its calls one after another; the spread of the counts is not modelled (the calls of one visit reach graph-store close together, and the model takes them as independent arrivals), which matters only when graph-store is busy (in simulations with up to 20 calls per visit and graph-store 30-60% busy the mean latency was within 2% on average). Calls lost from the capture, or sampled out, look the same as a count that varies: if the count should be fixed, check the exporters

calls the caller does not wait for (at least 95% of them start once the caller's span has ended, or outlive it on the caller's clock: fire and forget) are modelled as async: they load the callee, but the caller does not wait for them, so neither the callee's latency nor a change of it reaches the caller: events -> ledger (1 per visit), order -> audit (1 per visit), order -> events (1 per visit), partner -> ledger (1 per visit)

features calls feature-store 5 times at once (on 26% of its visits); feature-store has 2 workers and is 26% busy. The model takes the 5 calls as one batch: feature-store's arrivals as batches at Poisson epochs (an M^X/G/c queue, calls that arrive alone as batches of 1), and the wait for them as the time until the last of them is served
